correctness.rationale: All short signed-digit strings of each positive n obey the displayed last-digit bijections, with g(1)=g(2)=1 and n=1 exceptional case excluded. The 8-state invariant for v(n) follows from two unimodular matrices and exhaustive sign comparisons; its complete generating functions give the positive index count for every binary length. The adjacent cross-moment telescopes exactly to 1, yielding U_L=L and S_L=(3^(L-1)+1)/2 with base L=1. The independent checker enumerates representations through n=1300 and checks every dyadic position and the first two moments through L=16; the published proof, not finite tests, establishes all L.

originality.rationale: The closest public work identifies total short signed-digit counts (arXiv:2308.07448), the signed recurrence (OEIS A145865), fixed-length zero-digit weight polynomials (arXiv:2108.12417), and the Fibonacci zero set of this same signed imbalance (2026/11/2/SCOPE-fibonacci-law-for-parity-balanced-short-signed-binary-representa--c38bf7959659). The new claim is not the recurrence or zero count: it supplies the exact positive-sign count at every dyadic cutoff and exact first and squared moments, which are not stated by those inspected results. The eight-state sign refinement distinguishes signs deliberately collapsed in the four-state zero automaton. Prior formulas make these aggregates computable but do not express or directly dominate the new all-depth closed laws.
residual_risks: A signed-moment identity or sign-counting formula may be hidden in unindexed literature, the inaccessible full OEIS A145865 entry, or an unexamined appendix.

value.rationale: For an established natural class of signed integer representations, the parity of negative digits controls cancellation between two representation types. The theorem adds an exact sign histogram that separates positive/negative cases beyond the previously published Fibonacci neutral set, and exact first and second moments, showing an exponential-squared imbalance despite only logarithmic signed aggregate. These complementary statistics describe substantial structure for all binary lengths and provide benchmarks for finer signed-digit distributions; no external downstream theorem is asserted.
